deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and is not in Riemann's hand. It is the second page of an archival cover note dated 1897 (accession no. 4658). The note was written by M. Schering, the widow of Ernst Schering (1833–1897), Riemann's Göttingen colleague and later editor of Gauss's works. It continues her copy of a letter from her brother-in-law, Professor K. Schering, describing three fascicles in Ernst's handwriting.

The page first finishes the discussion of fascicles 1/ and 2/ ('Aetherbewegungen I/II'). K. Schering asks whether part of the existing material was worked out independently by Ernst, and judges that this can hardly be decided any more.

It then describes fascicle 3/: 'two sheets fastened together, headed "Hypothesen der Geometrie"', whose content relates to Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen'. The letter copy ends with '(gez.) K. Schering'.

M. Schering then adds her own postscript. She suggests that the manuscript 'Hypothesen der Geometrie' may contain independent investigations by her husband. She knows he made several such studies. She has also seen in his correspondence with H. von Helmholtz that he mentioned his own investigations in this field and submitted some of them to Helmholtz. This presumably refers to the 1868 Schering–Helmholtz exchange that followed Helmholtz's 'Über die Thatsachen, die der Geometrie zum Grunde liegen'. She signs 'M. Schering'.

The page's purpose is provenance and attribution. It warns that the following 'Aether' manuscripts, which are close to Riemann's published fragments on gravitation and light (Werke 1876, pp. 496–502), may be Ernst Schering's copies or reworkings rather than Riemann autographs. The next page indeed begins Ernst Schering's 'Aetherbewegungen I'. That page treats the potential V with ΔV = −4πρ, V → 0 at infinity, a velocity field equal to grad V, and irrotationality and divergence conditions; none of this appears on the present page.

results.what: Provenance note: the 'Aetherbewegungen I/II' and 'Hypothesen der Geometrie' manuscripts in this bundle are in Ernst Schering's hand, not Riemann's. They may contain Schering's own work, including investigations communicated to Helmholtz.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a 1897 cover letter by K. and M. Schering about manuscripts in Ernst Schering's hand. It contains no mathematics by Riemann. It is mildly interesting for provenance: it cautions that the 'Aether' fragments may be Schering's reworkings, and it mentions the Schering–Helmholtz correspondence on the foundations of geometry. It has no bearing on Riemann's mathematical priority.
transcription_corrections: The signature line reads '(gez.) K. Schering' (period after 'gez'), not '(gez:)'.
'Untersuchungen' in the line 'seine eigenen Untersuchungen' is written with its ending squeezed into the right margin; the reading is correct.
Otherwise the machine transcription matches the image; 'Habi=litationsschrift' is a line-break hyphenation with a double hyphen.
